_comment: Declares that this record's stored text CANNOT be honestly re-derived from its stored original. Checked and falsification-tested by scripts/derive_text.py.
not_derivable_reason:
The record's own `retrieved_by` says the text was 'extracted and CLEANED by operator' from the byte-exact official ST/SPACE/61/Rev.3 Russian edition. The cleaning is the obstacle. This volume separates paragraphs by FIRST-LINE INDENTATION rather than blank lines, and the indent values are not consistent — measured across section A of the French edition they run 13, 14, 18, 19, 20, 22, 23 and 24 columns, with article bodies and preambular paragraphs on different bases and ragged justification moving them by a column either way. No indent threshold separates a paragraph start from a wrapped continuation across the whole document, so the paragraph structure in the stored text reflects an operator's reading, not a rule. Reproducing it would mean declaring a literal anchor for most paragraphs in the instrument — a recipe that restates its own answer and proves nothing about the original. Refused deliberately.

Note this is a statement about the LAYOUT, not the text: the Russian text itself is authentic and hash-pinned, and extract.py measures its token overlap against the official PDF on every run.
_remedy: If the paragraph convention is ever identified as a rule rather than a series of readings, this becomes derivable and the declaration should be deleted.
